name: Bridge Pose
intro:
Bridge Pose (Setu Bandhasana) is a gentle backbend that strengthens the back, glutes, and legs while opening the chest and shoulders. In this pose, the body forms a bridge-like shape as the hips lift upward while the feet and shoulders remain grounded. It is commonly practiced as a preparatory pose for deeper backbends and is suitable for beginners.

Setu Bandhasana helps improve spinal flexibility and posture by counteracting the effects of prolonged sitting. It also stimulates the thyroid gland and improves blood circulation throughout the body. The expansion of the chest enhances lung capacity and promotes deeper breathing.

Regular practice of Bridge Pose helps reduce stress, calm the mind, and energize the body. It is especially beneficial for relieving mild back pain, strengthening the core and lower body, and improving overall stability and balance.

steps.text: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet placed hip-width apart.
Keep your arms beside your body with palms facing down.
Press your feet firmly into the mat.
Slowly lift your hips upward toward the ceiling.
Keep your thighs and knees aligned and parallel.
Clasp your hands under your back or keep arms pressing down.
Hold the pose while breathing steadily.

benefits: Strengthens the back, glutes, and legs
Stimulates abdominal organs and improves digestion
avoid: You have neck or spine injuries
You are suffering from severe back pain
You feel discomfort while lifting your hips
You have high blood pressure (consult a doctor before practice)
You have knee injuries (practice with caution)
